 Realty Income and NNN REIT yield about 6% and 6%, beating the 3.6% Social Security raise while paying out roughly 70% of cash flow. 
 Realty Income extends a 116-quarter dividend-raise streak, paying monthly with an AFFO payout near 73%, leaving a buffer after every check. 
 Apple Hospitality pays monthly with the widest cushion, distributing about 48% of cash flow, though hotel income can shrink fast when travel stops. 
 The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here . (Sponsor) 
 Real estate investment trusts have to pay out most of their taxable income as dividends to keep their tax-advantaged status, and that rule is why the sector creates the yields income investors come looking for. Whether a payout can last comes down to cash flow coverage, which means how much of a REIT's funds from operations (FFO) or adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) the dividend uses up. The 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment is 3.6%. That number is a percentage raise applied to a benefit you already collect. A dividend yield is a different measure: the annual cash a stock pays, stated as a share of its price. Each REIT below currently yields more than the COLA figure, and each one covers its distribution with cash flow to spare. 
 jetcityimage / iStock Editorial via Getty Images Realty Income: Monthly Checks With Coverage Behind Them 
 Realty Income ( NYSE:O ) is a retail net-lease REIT that owns freestanding commercial properties leased to operating businesses. It calls itself "The Monthly Dividend Company", and for a retiree paying monthly bills, that schedule matters. The trailing dividend yield is 5.22%. On the forward annualized dividend of $3.288 per share and a share price of $59.04, the forward yield works out to 5.57%, which puts Realty Income in high-yield territory.

 Dividend Safety Read 
 On coverage, third-quarter AFFO came in at $1.12 per share, up 3.7% from a year earlier, while monthly dividends paid during the quarter totaled $0.813 per share. That is an AFFO payout ratio of about 72.6%, leaving a buffer after every check goes out. Management also raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to $4.45 to $4.46 per share. On a free cash flow basis, the stock trades at 14 times free cash flow, a free cash flow yield of 6.90%. 
 The balance sheet is investment grade. Fitch assigned an 'A' rating with a Stable Outlook, and net debt to annualized pro forma adjusted EBITDAre was 5.4x at the end of the second quarter. The company expanded its revolving credit facility to $5.5 billion and says its equity needs for the rest of the year are already prefunded. 
 The track record is the best on this list. Realty Income announced its 116th consecutive quarterly dividend increase, which is its 136th raise since it listed on the NYSE in 1994. The latest declaration raised the monthly payment to $0.274 per share from $0.2715. 
 Why the Payout Should Hold 
 Realty Income keeps adding to its rent base at attractive spreads. During the quarter it invested $2.6 billion at a 6.8% initial weighted average cash yield, about 170 bps above its leverage-neutral cost of capital, and revenue rose 10.3% to $1.62 billion. For income investors, that spread is what pays for the small raises. 
 Risk to Weigh 
 Borrowing is getting more expensive. Interest expense rose to $333.6 million from $294.5 million. If rates stay high, more of each acquisition's return goes to lenders, and future dividend raises could stay small. 
 NNN REIT: Decades of Annual Raises on a Lean Payout 
 NNN REIT ( NYSE:NNN ) owns single-tenant retail properties on long-term net leases. Its biggest tenant groups are auto service shops and convenience stores. It pays quarterly. The forward annualized dividend is $2.48 per share, and at a share price of $41.96 that gives a forward yield of 5.91%. That is the highest current yield of the three, and it still counts as high-yield rather than ultra-high-yield. 
 Dividend Safety Read 
 NNN reported a 68% AFFO payout ratio for the third quarter, the lowest AFFO payout among these names. Third-quarter AFFO was $0.91 per share, up 5.8%, and Core FFO was $0.90 per share, up 5.9%. Full-year AFFO guidance stands at $3.55 to $3.59 per share, well above the annual dividend. The company has $1.4 billion of available liquidity. 
 NNN declared its 37th consecutive annual dividend increase this year. The dividend records confirm a steady rise: the quarterly payment was $0.50 in 2018 and 2019, moved to $0.58 in early 2025, then $0.60, and now $0.62. The records show quarterly payments going back to 1999. 
 Why the Payout Should Hold 
 NNN keeps buying property at yields that easily cover its funding costs. It closed $221.7 million of investments in the quarter at a 7.3% initial cash cap rate and has invested $658.1 million so far this year. Revenue rose 8.5% to $249.68 million. With roughly a third of AFFO kept after the dividend, NNN can pay for part of its growth without leaning on new shares or new debt. 
 Risk to Weigh 
 A bond comes due soon. NNN has $350 million of 3.600% notes maturing before year-end, and replacing low-coupon debt at today's rates raises interest costs, which leaves less room for future increases. 
 Apple Hospitality REIT: Monthly Hotel Income With the Widest Cushion 
 Apple Hospitality REIT ( NYSE:APLE ) is an equity REIT that owns 216 hotels with 29,459 guest rooms in 83 markets. They are mostly upscale, rooms-focused properties under the Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt brands. It pays monthly. The annualized distribution is $0.96 per share, and at a share price of $19.46 the forward yield is 4.93%. That makes it a high-yield name that pays out less of its cash flow than the other two. 
 Dividend Safety Read 
 Hotel REITs report modified funds from operations (MFFO), an FFO-based measure. Third-quarter MFFO was $0.50 per share, up 16.0%, against distributions of $0.24 per share paid during the quarter. That is an MFFO payout of about 48%, the most cash coverage in this group. 
 Leverage is low. Net debt is about 27.5% of total capitalization. The company amended its credit facility to roughly $1.3 billion, extended a $160 million term loan out to 2033 and repaid a $49.6 million mortgage, leaving 210 hotels unencumbered. 
 The record is good recently but has a gap further back. The monthly payment has been $0.08 per share without interruption since early 2024, with larger December payments of $0.13 in 2023 and 2024. During 2021, though, the payment was just $0.01 per share. A hotel REIT's payout can shrink fast when travel stops. 
 Why the Payout Should Hold 
 Cash flow is rising. Adjusted EBITDAre increased 13.3% to $139.7 million, and management raised its full-year Adjusted EBITDAre guidance to $482 million to $493 million. Chief Executive Justin Knight said "sustained demand momentum and muted new supply create a meaningful tailwind for our portfolio" heading into 2027. The company also has $242.5 million left under its share repurchase program. 
 Risk to Weigh 
 Hotel revenue resets every night. The company lists government shutdowns and travel disruptions among its risks, and a drop in business or leisure travel would hit Apple Hospitality's cash flow much sooner than a long-term lease would hit Realty Income or NNN. 
 Who These Three REITs Suit 
 These three names suit retirees and near-retirees who want rental-backed income on top of a Social Security check that will rise 3.6% next year. Realty Income offers the deepest raise history and monthly payments. NNN offers the highest current yield on a 68% AFFO payout. Apple Hospitality adds monthly hotel income with the widest cash coverage of the group. Together they make a well-covered income stream for an investor who values a dependable distribution more than a headline yield.
